sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in F.I.R. No.613 of 2022, under sections 376, 302, 201,
404, 411 of I.P.C., Police Station-Kotwali Nagar, District-Faizabad/Ayodhya.
3.  In terms of the F.I.R. it was initially registered under section 366 of I.P.C.

It was alleged that the sister of the informant, who was aged about 20 years, was working in a retail shop of Vishal Mega Mart, Civil Line, Faizabad and on 27.08.2022 she had gone to work there, however, she did not return back.
It was alleged that she had left the Mega Mart at 8.17 p.m. and it was apprehended that Anoop Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Subsequently, the applicant was linked with the offence in question based upon the statement of Assistant Manager of the Vishal Mega Mart, who has stated that she had left at 8.17 p.m. on 27.08.2022 and after leaving the Vishal Mega Mart she had gone to a chat shop and thereafter she went on e-rickshaw.
As the applicant is alleged to be the owner of the e-rickshaw driver, he was apprehended.

Counsel for the applicant argues that also in terms of the investigation, the call detail records of the applicant were shown near the place of the incident,
however, the CDR could not match with the record of the deceased so as to link the applicant with the offence in question.
He further argues that skeleton of the deceased was recovered and the post-mortem report on record could not ascertain the cause of death.
He,thus, argues that the applicant should be enlarged on bail as the applicant has no criminal history.
4. Learned A.G.A. strongly opposes the bail application by arguing that skeleton was recovered at the instance and pointing out of the applicant.
An Aadhar Card, Identity Card and clothes were also recovered at the instance and pointing out of the applicant.
He, thus, argued that there was sufficient material to link the applicant with the offence in question.
Thus, he argues that the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
5. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie the applicant is linked with the offence in question based upon the last seen theory and recovery as argued by the learned A.G.A.
, the last seen theory alone is not enough to link applicant with the offence in question as the CDR of both the phones are primarily not available to link the applicant with the offence.

The alleged recovery is also not in the presence of any independent witnesses and thus there was non-compliance of mandate of section 100 of Cr.P.C.
6.

Considering the above referred facts coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that if the applicant is enlarged on bail, he can adversely affect the trial.
The applicant is in custody since 18.09.2022.
The Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
